facts.value: next regular payday or 21 days after discharge, whichever occurs last
facts.summary: Tennessee: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due next regular payday or 21 days after discharge, whichever occurs last.
facts.evidence_quote: Any employee who leaves or is discharged from employment shall be paid in full all wages or salary earned by the employee no later than the next regular pay day following the date of dismissal or voluntary leaving, or twenty-one (21) days following the date of discharge or voluntary leaving, whichever occurs last. There is no exemption under the law. Tenn. Code. Ann. 50-2-103 (g)
facts.source_title: Wages & Breaks (Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development)
facts.source_publisher: Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development
facts.notes: Tennessee payday rules apply to private employers with 5 or more employees (same page).

facts.value: next regular payday or 21 days after leaving, whichever occurs last
facts.summary: Tennessee: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next regular payday or 21 days after leaving, whichever occurs last.
facts.evidence_quote: Any employee who leaves or is discharged from employment shall be paid in full all wages or salary earned by the employee no later than the next regular pay day following the date of dismissal or voluntary leaving, or twenty-one (21) days following the date of discharge or voluntary leaving, whichever occurs last. There is no exemption under the law. Tenn. Code. Ann. 50-2-103 (g)
facts.source_title: Wages & Breaks (Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development)
facts.source_publisher: Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development

facts.value: No state minimum wage law (federal $7.25 applies to FLSA-covered employers)
facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Tennessee basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: No state minimum wage law (federal $7.25 applies to FLSA-covered employers).
facts.evidence_quote: No state minimum wage law. Employers subject to the Fair Labor Standards Act must pay the current Federal minimum wage of $7.25 per hour.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Tennessee independent contractor reporting required? (per OCSE): No
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Tennessee new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Within 20 days of hire date
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Within 20 days of hire date
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Tennessee: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Semi-monthly.
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.value: At least once per month; employers with 5 or more employees must keep regular paydays
facts.summary: Tennessee pay frequency rule: At least once per month; employers with 5 or more employees must keep regular paydays.
facts.evidence_quote: Private employers with 5 or more employees are required to establish and maintain regular pay days. Employees are required to be paid at least once per month.
facts.source_publisher: Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development

facts.summary: Tennessee is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.applies_to: Effective July 2026 (DOL publication); Rate year July 1 - June 30 (DOL footnote 8)
facts.summary: Tennessee base new employer UI rate: 2.70%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. Rate basis: DOL base rate. It may exclude mandatory surcharges, fund-building rates and assessments; check the state agency or total_new_employer_rate where available.

facts.applies_to: Effective July 2026 (DOL publication); Rate year July 1 - June 30 (DOL footnote 8)
facts.summary: Tennessee experience-rated UI tax rates range from 0.01% to 10.00%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026

facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes.
